title: Homotopy equivalent two-term complexes: A_1 + B_0 is isomorphic to B_1 + A_0
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $d_A:A_1\to A_0$ and $d_B:B_1\to B_0$ be homomorphisms of $R$-modules. Suppose given $R$-linear maps $\varphi_i:A_i\to B_i$ and $\psi_i:B_i\to A_i$ ($i=0,1$) with $d_B\circ\varphi_1=\varphi_0\circ d_A$ and $d_A\circ\psi_1=\psi_0\circ d_B$, and $R$-linear maps $h:A_0\to A_1$ and $h':B_0\to B_1$ with $$\mathrm{id}_{A_1}-\psi_1\circ\varphi_1=h\circ d_A,\quad\mathrm{id}_{A_0}-\psi_0\circ\varphi_0=d_A\circ h,\quad\mathrm{id}_{B_1}-\varphi_1\circ\psi_1=h'\circ d_B,\quad\mathrm{id}_{B_0}-\varphi_0\circ\psi_0=d_B\circ h'.$$ Then $A_1\oplus B_0\cong B_1\oplus A_0$ as $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S3 (lemma-sum-two-terms, line 35709) and its proof (the 2x2 matrix identity, lines 35721-35754). Tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags: 00S3,algebra-lemma-sum-two-terms.

proof.text: Write $P=A_1\oplus B_0$ and $Q=B_1\oplus A_0$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Define $R$-linear maps $C:P\to Q$ and $D:Q\to P$ by $C(a,b)=(\varphi_1(a)-h'(b),d_A(a)+\psi_0(b))$ and $D(c,e)=(\psi_1(c)+h(e),-d_B(c)+\varphi_0(e))$. These are the two $2\times2$ matrices in the proof of Stacks 00S3, with rows and columns ordered as the displayed summands.

For $(a,b)\in P$, expand $DC(a,b)$. Its first component is $\psi_1\varphi_1(a)-\psi_1h'(b)+hd_A(a)+h\psi_0(b)=a+(h\psi_0-\psi_1h')(b)$ by $\mathrm{id}_{A_1}-\psi_1\varphi_1=hd_A$. Its second component is $-d_B\varphi_1(a)+d_Bh'(b)+\varphi_0d_A(a)+\varphi_0\psi_0(b)=b$ by $d_B\varphi_1=\varphi_0d_A$ and $\mathrm{id}_{B_0}-\varphi_0\psi_0=d_Bh'$. Thus $DC=U_P$, where $U_P(a,b)=(a+u(b),b)$ and $u=h\psi_0-\psi_1h'$. Reversing the roles gives $CD=U_Q$: its components on $(c,e)\in Q$ are $\varphi_1\psi_1(c)+h'd_B(c)+(\varphi_1h-h'\varphi_0)(e)=c+v(e)$ and $d_A\psi_1(c)-\psi_0d_B(c)+d_Ah(e)+\psi_0\varphi_0(e)=e$, where $v=\varphi_1h-h'\varphi_0$. The first equality uses $\mathrm{id}_{B_1}-\varphi_1\psi_1=h'd_B$; the second uses $d_A\psi_1=\psi_0d_B$ and $\mathrm{id}_{A_0}-\psi_0\varphi_0=d_Ah$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S3 (lemma-sum-two-terms), proof, matrix identity, lines 35734-35754; the reverse product is checked explicitly here

proof.text: The triangular maps have explicit inverses: $U_P^{-1}(a,b)=(a-u(b),b)$ and $U_Q^{-1}(c,e)=(c-v(e),e)$. Hence $L=U_P^{-1}D:Q\to P$ satisfies $LC=\mathrm{id}_P$, while $T=DU_Q^{-1}:Q\to P$ satisfies $CT=\mathrm{id}_Q$. Then $L=L(CT)=(LC)T=T$, so $C$ is an $R$-linear isomorphism $P\cong Q$ with inverse $L=T$. This is the claimed $A_1\oplus B_0\cong B_1\oplus A_0$.
